title: Asymptotic permanental dominance at fixed Gram rank
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. The permanent of a matrix is the determinant without minus signs. For a table of inner products of n vectors (a positive semidefinite Gram matrix), the permutations of the vectors split into symmetry types, one for each Young diagram with n boxes, and each type has a positive semidefinite matrix block; the all-symmetric type gives exactly the permanent. Lieb's permanental dominance conjecture (1966), restricted to the ordinary immanants, says that the average eigenvalue of every block is at most the permanent; Lavi's quadratic conjecture (2026) says the same for the mean square of the eigenvalues. The stronger permanent-on-top conjecture is false, so these averaged inequalities are what may survive.

What was known. Lieb's version for ordinary immanants holds for n ≤ 15 (Pate; Li) and for all n at Gram rank at most three (Pate 1999, Theorem 2); Pate's Theorem 4 gives eventual dominance for the shapes (n+s, nk). Lavi proved the quadratic version for n ≤ 5. At real rank two both hold for every n, by the rank-two permanent-on-top theorem.

Results. Fix the Gram rank d. Both normalised moments tend to zero as n → ∞, uniformly over all non-trivial irreducible representations of Sn and all inputs of rank at most d, so both inequalities hold at each fixed rank for all sufficiently large n. The threshold n0(d) is not computed and no new case of finite order is claimed. For the quadratic inequality this is new at every complex rank d ≥ 2 and real rank d ≥ 3; for ordinary immanants it is new from rank four, and there only for four-row shapes with λ4 ≥ 3 and λ2 > λ3 (everything else at rank at most four is due to Pate). The standard representation is eventually the worst case; at complex rank d its largest first and second moments are asymptotic to (d−1) log n / n and (d−1)(log n)2/n. Both moments still tend to zero when d log n = o(√n), and the first moment does whenever d log n = o(n). For the standard representation alone, explicit bounds hold for every n and d (first moment at most (6√(e n d) − 1)/(n − 1)).

Method. Each block's trace is bounded by an ordered-partition matrix whose trace is estimated by Gaussian averaging; a new strict inequality for expected logarithms of sums of exponential variables shows that the dimension of the representation outgrows this bound when two rows of the diagram are long; diagrams with one dominant row are handled by counting; the standard shape uses the sharp Bapat–Sunder growth of the earlier Evidence Press release 10.5281/zenodo.24509057.

Limits. The threshold order is not computed, so no individual finite case is settled. Only the symmetric-group (immanant) form of Lieb's conjecture is treated, not the subgroup form. Real-rank constants are known only up to a factor.

Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF), a Python standard-library script that checks the ingredients of the proofs on explicit finite examples (exact arithmetic for the algebraic identities, floating point with a declared tolerance for the analytic inequalities) and its recorded output, plus the bibliography, a machine-readable index, a research-gate record, a review summary, a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. The script exits with an error on any failed check, also under python -O.

Assurance. Written proofs; the script checks ingredients and is not part of any proof. Internal AI-assisted review only: a combined five-role Claude review panel, a proof audit of every proof by the lead, one revision round, a verification re-review with a proof audit of the new and rewritten proofs, and a clean replay with a negative control. No Astra/Codex review took place. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
